newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ALP PROMISES EQUAL LOCAL CALL PRICES IN BUSH
The Federal Opposition says it would legislate for equal prices for local phone calls in the city and the bush.
The A-L-P also plans to ensure that broad banded services are available to all Australians regardless of where they live.
The initiatives were announced yesterday after the Federal Shadow Cabinet met in Ballarat during a two-day visit.
Party leader Kim Beazley says amendments would be made to current legislation to ensure price discrimination didn't occur between city and country telecommunication services.
CYCLONE HAROLD NOW CATEGORY TWO
In Queensland, the Weather Bureau says Tropical Cyclone Harold, which intensified overnight, won't threaten the eastcoast for at least two more days.
The category two cyclone which formed in the Coral Sea early yesterday, is about 800 kilometres east-north-east of Bowen, and moving slowly south-south-west.
The Bureau's Jeff Callaghan he expects Harold to move south, then east, then become stationary.
LOWER INTEREST RATES HELPING JOBS GROWTH
There's new evidence that lower interest rates are now having an impact on the employment plans of Australian companies.
Recruitment firm Morgan and Banks is predicting the strongest period of jobs growth for a year and a half in the three months ahead.
Its latest Job Index indicates nearly 36 per cent of organisations intend to increase their workforce before the end of April, while only 15 per cent are planning to cut back.
Head of economic research, John Winter, says the revised Budget forecast for 8.5 per cent unemployment by June could well be met as the Reserve Bank's interest rate cuts work through the economy.
FUNEL-WEB FARM TO PROVIDE ANTIVENOM SUPPLIES
A program to breed the deadly funnel-web spider has begun in New South Wales, in an attempt to provide a long-term supply of antivenom to hospitals throughout Australia.
The Australian Reptile Park on the Central Coast has begun successfully breeding the poisonous spider to be milked for the antitoxin.
Park representative, Mary Rayner, says the action is in response to a recent shortage of funnelwebs, which caused a drop in antivenom supplies.
VIETNAM REFUSES TO PUT HUMAN RIGHTS ON TALKS AGENDA
Vietnam's Foreign Minister, Nguyen Manh Cam, says Australia can not impose its human rights values on Vietnam.
Mr Cam will today meet the Prime Minister, John Howard, to complete a round of talks in Canberra.
A spokesman for Mr Cam says human rights issues were not the point of last night's talks with Australia's Foreign Minister, Alexander Downer.
This is despite reports of the meeting saying there was substantive discussion on human rights and religious freedom in Vietnam.
However, Mr Cam did endorse Australia's push to have Mr Howard attend next year's Asia-Europe leaders' summit.
He said Hanoi was consistent in backing Australia's involvement in Asia.
